blocks.title: Investigation Data Sources and Evidence comparison
Investigation Data Sources and Evidence exam shortcuts
items: Need to know what weakness attacker may have exploited → VULNERABILITY SCAN
Compare incident timing with known vulnerabilities and misconfigurations.
Example: A scan shows the compromised server was missing a critical patch.
Need quick recurring summary → AUTOMATED REPORT
Use generated reports for routine findings and trends.
Example: A daily SIEM report lists top alerts.
Dashboards summarize current security posture visually.
Example: SOC dashboard shows active incidents and alert counts.
Need exact network conversation details → PACKET CAPTURE
Packet captures provide the deepest network-level evidence.
Example: Inspect a PCAP to see DNS queries and HTTP request details.
Need full traffic content but only have NetFlow-style data → YOU NEED PACKET CAPTURE
Flow metadata does not contain packet payloads.
Example: Use PCAP when you must inspect the actual protocol exchange.
blocks.example: Choose the source that provides the most direct evidence for the investigation question.

questions.q: An investigator wants to determine whether a compromised server was missing a known critical patch before the incident. Which source is most useful?
questions.explanation: Vulnerability scans identify missing patches, known flaws, and misconfigurations.

questions.q: A SOC manager wants a machine-generated daily summary of the highest-severity alerts. Which source best fits?
questions.explanation: Automated reports provide recurring machine-generated summaries.

questions.q: An analyst wants an at-a-glance view of active incidents and alert counts. Which source is best?
questions.explanation: Dashboards visually summarize status, metrics, and trends.

questions.q: An investigator needs to inspect the exact DNS queries and HTTP request details exchanged over the network. Which source is best?
questions.explanation: Packet captures provide detailed packet-level evidence and may include traffic contents.

questions.q: An analyst only has NetFlow-style metadata but needs to inspect the actual protocol payload. What additional source is required?
questions.explanation: Flow metadata does not contain packet payloads; a packet capture is needed for full packet inspection.
